proposal.name: flatten-garment
proposal.purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment while ensuring reachability compromises never reverse the verified opening direction, and while distinguishing a separable free edge from a soft interior fold before pulling.
proposal.guidance: Add two decision rules to the existing staged workflow. First, when choosing an anchor, prefer a boundary where the garment silhouette meets bare table (a free hem, cuff, or corner) over a high-contrast line in the interior of the fabric: an interior line is often a soft fold of the same layer, and pinching it gathers cloth into a roll instead of separating a layer. Treat a thin, low-relief local measurement as evidence of a single surface, not as evidence that the surface is separable. Second, when the direction that the scene verifies as opening is blocked by reach or workspace limits, do not substitute a pull toward the garment's own mass just because that region is reachable; pulling inward raises local relief and overlap. Instead keep the opening axis and re-anchor on the opposite side of the garment, or reposition the garment, so the same axis becomes reachable. After the reversible probe segment, abort and re-plan if fabric gathers toward the garment centroid, if the silhouette does not grow, or if peak relief rises, rather than continuing into laydown.
proposal.rationale: This run failed in exactly these two ways: an interior fold line was mistaken for a separable layer boundary, and the reachable substitute direction pointed into the garment body, so the action ended with a rolled tube, higher relief, and an unchanged footprint. Both rules are general to reach-limited single-arm opening attempts and are not covered explicitly by the current skill text.

proposal.name: laydown
proposal.purpose: Convert a garment held from a useful lifting anchor into a more spread tabletop configuration, ensuring the deposited section extends the footprint instead of re-piling on the garment it came from.
proposal.guidance: Keep the existing quasi-static procedure, then add a footprint rule for the release phase. Before releasing, judge the hanging length of the lifted section and choose a release point on clean surface that lies outside the garment's current footprint by at least that length; releasing inside or just at the edge of the footprint lets the section fall back onto its own mass and create a new fold ridge instead of an extension. Treat footprint growth as the release criterion: if a short probe segment shows the silhouette is not extending toward clean surface, continue transporting or re-plan rather than releasing. When reachable clean surface is smaller than the hanging length, prefer laying the section along the roll or limb's long axis so it unfolds lengthwise, and accept a partial deposit rather than stacking it back over the body.

The existing skill says to release quasi-statically on a clean surface but gives no footprint-relative distance criterion, which is exactly the missing decision here.

proposal.purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting in a verified opening direction, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
proposal.guidance:
Follow this staged workflow:
1. Acquire a validated garment structure: choose a visible, liftable anchor whose local RGB-D measurement, height, and depth consistency support a real garment grasp; do not proceed from an unsupported or table-only point.
2. Establish a hanging configuration if useful: lift to a validated safe height and confirm that the grasped fabric is supported and can hang without dragging or colliding. If the lift does not reveal a supported structure, stop and re-plan.
3. Transport toward a verified opening direction: infer the direction from the current garment geometry and before/after evidence. Use validated intermediate waypoints with stable orientation and workspace margin. The transport direction should move away from concentrated fabric mass or bundled regions. Do not assume any single direction is universally correct; adapt to visible garment configuration.
4. Continue only while overlap decreases or coverage increases: after each meaningful transport segment, compare the garment footprint, visible area, layer overlap, and height relief. Stop, release, or re-plan when the move is not improving those measures; never continue a blind pull.
5. Lay down progressively: retreat while descending through validated intermediate heights, release quasi-statically on a clean surface, and avoid dropping, flinging, twisting, or dragging the loaded gripper. The skill supplies this decision sequence, never fixed coordinates or robot API calls.

The before/after comparison shows successful flattening when pulling away from the bundled core mass. The original flatten-garment guidance stated 'The farthest safe X direction is allowed only when the scene verifies that it opens the garment' but this phrasing could be misinterpreted as X being privileged. The modification clarifies that transport direction should be inferred from visible geometry by moving away from concentrated regions, with no directional bias. All other workflow stages (validated acquisition, hanging configuration, progressive monitoring, quasi-static laydown) remain unchanged and are strongly supported by this successful outcome.

proposal.name: drag-versus-unfold-check

proposal.guidance: After a transport segment, compare how the far boundary of the garment moved against how the anchored features on the opposite side moved. When both move together by a similar amount, the pull is sliding the whole garment and the bite is coupled to lower layers: pause, restore a supported hanging configuration with more vertical clearance, and let the held layer separate before resuming lateral motion. When the pulled boundary advances much further than the opposite side and previously hidden surface becomes exposed, the pull is genuinely separating layers and should continue in the same direction with more travel until the fold lip flattens or improvement stops. Treat a remaining standing fold lip, an overhanging rolled edge, or a shadow gap under cloth as evidence that transport ended early rather than as evidence of a bad direction, and preserve the validated grasp anchor and bite depth in that case.

proposal.guidance: Keep the existing translation-only detection and re-anchoring logic, and add two checks when reading the after state. First, do not score a lower height profile as progress on its own: a whole-bundle carry can settle flatter while previously visible interior evidence, such as a lining patch, print area, care label, or a visible opening, disappears. Treat the loss of such interior features as closure rather than opening, and require newly exposed interior fabric or reduced layer overlap before calling the move an improvement. Second, before reusing an image-space heading, confirm the assumed correspondence between image directions and robot travel directions against the displacement actually observed in the previous before/after pair; if the mass moved in a different image sense than predicted, treat the heading as unverified and re-derive it rather than repeating or extending it.
proposal.rationale: This iteration produced a large coherent translation with reduced relief, which looks like progress, yet the interior green patch and label became hidden and no new print appeared, and the observed displacement direction contradicted the planned mapping. Both are reusable evaluation cautions not covered by the current skill text.

proposal.name: flatten-garment
proposal.purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting far enough in a verified opening direction to actually unfold cloth, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
proposal.guidance: Keep the existing staged workflow and sharpen the transport stage. Size the transport distance to the garment's own characteristic span rather than to a small fraction of the clear table: a short conservative retreat after a validated lift tends to smooth surface relief and slightly lengthen the footprint while leaving layer overlap untouched, which reads as progress but does not open the garment. Treat the pattern of lower relief plus slightly larger footprint plus unchanged overlap as evidence that travel was too short, not that the anchor was wrong, and extend travel along the same verified direction before considering a new anchor. Gate the descent on an observation taken while the cloth is still raised, so the decision to lay down or to keep travelling is made from what is actually hanging rather than from the commanded plan.
proposal.rationale: This run validated the anchor and grasp depth yet still produced only smoothing, because the retreat was chosen as a fraction of free table instead of being scaled to how much cloth needed to unfold. The existing skill says to continue while overlap decreases but gives no way to size the first transport segment, so a short pull looks compliant while being physically unable to separate layers.

proposal.name: flatten-garment
proposal.purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting in a verified opening direction, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
proposal.guidance:
Follow this staged workflow:
1. Acquire a validated garment structure: choose a visible, liftable anchor whose local RGB-D measurement, height, and depth consistency support a real garment grasp; do not proceed from an unsupported or table-only point.
2. Establish a hanging configuration if useful: lift to a validated safe height and confirm that the grasped fabric is supported and can hang without dragging or colliding. When opposition is required, deliberately keep the lift low so distant material stays weighted on the table. If the lift does not reveal a supported structure, stop and re-plan.
3. Transport toward a verified opening direction: infer the direction from the current garment geometry and before/after evidence, then use validated intermediate waypoints with stable orientation and workspace margin. The farthest safe X or Y direction is allowed only when the scene verifies that it opens the garment; do not assume any compass direction is always correct.
4. Continue only while overlap decreases or coverage increases: after each meaningful transport segment, compare the garment footprint, visible area, layer overlap, and height relief. Recognize that successful execution of all stages—confirmed grasp of intended structure, target-layer lift with opposition maintained, transport in planned direction, controlled laydown on clear surface—combined with an after-state showing the deposited material settled back near (not beyond) the previously exposed features, indicates stroke length was insufficient to clear the spatial overlap even though the mechanics and direction were correct. In that case extend pull_distance substantially (50-70% longer) from the same validated anchor and direction, because the roll or fold needs to travel farther to unroll and reveal new fabric regions rather than settling back into overlap. Confirm the extension is evidence-based: when the after-state shows new fabric features exposed at the grasp site (proving the target layer was moved) but the deposited outline has not extended the garment boundary in the transport direction and no new distant regions are revealed, the stroke was mechanically sound but spatially short. Stop, release, or re-plan when a move actively worsens those measures, when the grasp fails to acquire the intended structure, or when distant landmarks start moving with the grasp indicating body-continuous hold.
5. Lay down progressively: retreat while descending through validated intermediate heights, release quasi-statically on a clean surface, and avoid dropping, flinging, twisting, or dragging the loaded gripper. The skill supplies this decision sequence, never fixed coordinates or robot API calls.
proposal.rationale: Run-level synthesis from 13 provisional observation(s). This iteration produced exactly the ambiguous case the current step 4 does not cover: coverage did not grow, yet the dome relief collapsed and hidden print cells appeared. Without this rule the outcome reads as a translation-only result and invites an unnecessary re-anchor, discarding a bite that demonstrably enclosed the covering layer. This run had repeatedly diagnosed whole-body drags, where the outline relocated congruently and the origin was left bare. This iteration produced the opposite signature from a short gated probe: fixed distant landmarks plus newly exposed print. Without an explicit rule, that outcome risks being read as a null or insufficient result and answered by another re-anchor, discarding a validated anchor and bite. The rule makes the distinction reusable and ties the extension to a safer deposit. This iteration extended a stroke on the assumption that more distance would prevent drape-back, but the result was another translated copy of the outline plus a garment cropped by the bottom edge of one view and the bottom and right edges of the other, so neither the footprint nor the uncovering could be measured. The reusable lesson is to bound stroke and deposit by observability, which the current skill does not state.

proposal.name: laydown
proposal.purpose: Convert a garment held from a useful lifting anchor into a more spread tabletop configuration, and recognise when a release has re-piled the garment onto itself instead of opening it.
proposal.guidance: Keep the quasi-static procedure: let the garment hang under gravity, retreat away from the hanging cloth while descending through intermediate heights, let the hanging face become the upward face, and release in a controlled way. Add three checks. First, before descending, require the retreat to carry the grasp point beyond the horizontal extent of the material still hanging below it, onto clear table, so the fabric unrolls onto bare surface rather than settling back over the area it came from; a retreat shorter than the hanging garment's own reach should be treated as not ready for release. Second, when the transported material is a covering layer that has been peeled off another part of the garment, judge the deposit against the newly uncovered region, not only against the garment's previous outline: require the grasp to have retreated far enough that the whole length of ply trailing behind the jaws will land beyond the edge of the freshly exposed area on clear surface, because a long peeled band keeps its tail near the origin and will drape back over the uncovered feature as it lowers if the retreat is measured only against the old footprint. Third, after release, compare footprints and check uncovered features specifically: if the deposited outline sits inside the previous outline, if previously exposed features such as prints, collars or hems have become covered, if the trailing end of a peeled layer has settled back across the region it was pulled off, and if new steep fold walls appear in depth, judge the laydown a regression caused by too short a retreat, and plan the next deposit farther out across clean table instead of repeating the same descent from the same anchor.

Existing laydown guidance covers retreat length and footprint comparison but says nothing about preserving observability of the deposit, which is what limited this evaluation. This run's peel succeeded in uncovering several previously hidden print tiles, yet the trailing end of the deposited layer still lies across the right edge of that newly exposed print in both camera views. The existing laydown guidance only requires the deposit to leave the previous outline, which this release satisfied while still partially undoing the peel, so the release criterion needs to reference the uncovered feature and the length of the carried material. This iteration provides direct evidence that retreat distance must account for peeled layer length plus newly uncovered feature extent, not just the original garment footprint. However, the after images show the deposited ply's trailing end draped back over the center print area that had been uncovered during transport, with Camera B RGB clearly showing dark fabric lying across the print and Camera B depth showing new elevated relief over that region. The retreat (~200mm) exceeded the garment's old outline but not the combined reach of the carried band plus the print block it had peeled off. This failure signature—successful peel followed by re-covering during laydown—proves that v2 guidance needs a second distance test specifically for peeled layers, and that both the hanging material's reach and the uncovered feature's extent must be cleared.

The existing skill judges deposits only by footprint comparison and by retreating farther across clean table, which is exactly what caused the loss of observability here. 此迭代表现出完美的机械执行：边缘抓取成功，对抗得到验证（印刷标记保持静止），运输受控，分阶段释放准静态，框架正确。但任务进展有限：衣物从右下移到中上，堆变得更紧凑，但没有袖子展开到桌面上。after视图在两个摄像头中都显示仍然是堆叠配置，没有新的展开区域。这证明了准静态沉积本身不足以展开：方向很重要。当沉积将边缘拉回到堆上方时，它会收紧而不是展开；当横向拉离时，它应该剥离。laydown技能应该识别这种'机械上完美但几何上中性'的结果，并引导下一次尝试改变方向和距离而不是放弃已验证的抓取策略。 此次迭代提供了laydown成功展开衣物的首个清晰证据：袖子从堆上横向剥离并沉积到新桌面区域，足迹向右扩展，绿色印花条更加暴露，凸起带高度下降。这与之前的全等平移(迭代2-5)形成对比，那些只是重新定位了堆。区别在于运输方向(横向离开堆vs向上回到堆中心)。该模式现在可以被编码为识别laydown何时实际实现展开任务，而不仅仅是机械正确。

proposal.name: null-change-missed-grasp-recovery
proposal.purpose: 识别近零变化衣物动作，并在清洁空抓发生时分离夹爪未达表面与锚点不可咬合两种情况，选择对应的恢复策略
proposal.guidance: 保留现有的清洁未命中和接触-未抓握两个分支。添加清洁空抓诊断规则：当衣物轮廓、所有地标和目标区域在整个rollout中完全不变，无局部下沉、无提升时悬挂材料、无横向运输时的拖拽或滑动，且释放时无材料落下，判定为清洁空抓。此时分两种情况：(1)若计划闭合高度低于测量表面但夹爪运动学下限高于该表面，说明夹爪物理上无法到达，需改选浮雕更高的边界锚点使其自身高度超过夹爪下限；(2)若闭合高度在可达范围内，说明锚点虽有浮雕但是无可分离边界的宽阔侧面，夹爪闭合时只能压迫而非夹持，需改选该结构的可追踪自由边缘如遮挡边、袖口、下摆，那里有可独立咬合的层边界。两种情况下运输方向、运输距离、下降阶段和释放机制都未被测试，保持不变。与接触-未抓握的区别是：接触-未抓握会在闭合点看到局部下沉，清洁空抓则完全无响应。
proposal.rationale: Run-level synthesis from 4 provisional observation(s). This run shows a failure mode the current skill only names but does not operationalise: a fully null scene with no slump, caused by a commanded closing height above the measured surface and an anchor placed off the named target. Adding the in-air branch and the anchor-on-named-structure check prevents repeating a blind pull and prevents discarding transport parameters that were never exercised. 两次连续的空中未接触（迭代2和3）表明需要一个专门的分支来处理高度参考失败与锚点位置不确定性的组合，现有技能的接触但未抓握分支涵盖了软堆压缩但未通过下陷特征捕获完全未接触的情况 This iteration lowered the closing height further below the measured local surface than the previous flank attempt and still produced a bit-for-bit unchanged scene in both RGB views, both depth views and every rollout tile. That distinguishes a genuine depth problem from an anchor-class problem, which the existing skill does not separate, and it prevents further iterations from spending attempts on incremental depth changes at points that cannot be enclosed at all.

proposal.name: translation-only-reanchor
proposal.purpose: Recognise that measured height above the table does not by itself prove a graspable ply, and separate a drag-without-lift outcome from a genuine transport failure before any pull parameter is changed.
proposal.guidance: Keep the existing stop rule for repeated congruent relocations, the boundary-verification requirements, and the reachability gate. Add a clause that verified relief is not verified ply: an anchor may sit clearly above the table and still be a broad compressible flank with no free edge, in which case closing near the measured surface only pinches the top face and the tool drags the whole garment. Require two things before the approach is accepted. First, the closing height must be referenced to reach at or below the local fabric surface rather than standing just above it, because a soft fold sinks under the closing jaws. Second, the anchor must be a boundary of the named structure whose opening or whose two faces can be followed separately, such as a cuff mouth or a hem edge, in preference to any raised flank however tall. Then treat the post-lift hold check as an abort gate: if the outline and the landmarks far from the grasp stay pressed and unmoved, release quasi-statically and re-anchor, and record that transport direction, transport distance, descent staging and release remain untested so they are not revised on this evidence.
proposal.rationale: Run-level synthesis from 3 provisional observation(s). This run again produced a congruent relocation, but the cause was a candidate point at table-level height that the gripper's own height limit prevented it from enclosing. The existing skill covers congruent relocations and opening verification, yet nothing in the library tells the planner to reject an anchor as unreachable-for-gripping before committing, which is the reusable lesson here. This iteration corrected the previous table-level anchor by choosing a point with confirmed relief above the table, yet the outcome was again a congruent whole-garment shift shorter than commanded with no hanging fabric in any rollout frame. That shows the existing height-based reachability gate is insufficient on its own and needs the free-ply requirement and a surface-referenced closing height attached to it, so future attempts stop re-tuning the pull after an acquisition-stage failure. This run produced a near-congruent relocation together with a modest increase in exposed print, a combination the current skill does not cover; without an explicit rule the exposure gain invites crediting ply isolation and revising transport parameters that were never exercised.
